# v3.11-dev

Stronger protection against injected scripts. This is the change the previous
two releases were building towards.

## What's new

- **Training Tracker now tells your browser to run only the scripts Training
  Tracker itself put on the page.** Anything else — a `<script>` block or an
  `onclick` that somehow found its way into a page — is treated as plain text
  and does not run. This is the single biggest protection against a whole class
  of web attack, and it closes the last open item from the security review.

- **You should not notice any difference.** Every page, chart, report, export,
  the help window and the colour picker were checked and behave exactly as
  before. Every script the app legitimately loads is tagged with a one-time
  value the browser verifies; anything untagged is refused.

## If something does misbehave

An administrator can restore the previous behaviour immediately — no rebuild,
just a setting and a restart:

```
echo 'CSP_MODE=legacy' >> /opt/training-tracker/.env
systemctl restart training-tracker
```

The setting survives updates, so it stays in effect until you remove it. Full
instructions are under Troubleshooting in the README. Please do report it if you
need to use this — a page that requires the old behaviour is a bug worth fixing
properly rather than living with.

## Scope

This change covers **scripts only**. Styling rules are unchanged, and the
appearance of the app is not affected.
